How we handle eBilling and A/R

We support law-firm billing teams today. Our plan is to bring eBilling and accounts receivable together as one managed service, run partly by AI finance agents and priced on how quickly clients pay (Frontline growth plan).

Why billing needs attention now

  • Corporate clients increasingly use AI to review legal invoices.
  • That review has pushed invoice rejection rates from 11% to 18% (Frontline growth plan).
  • Each rejection slows cash collection and adds rework for the firm's billing staff.

What the service will look like

ElementHow it works
ScopeeBilling submission, rejection handling and A/R follow-up in one service
DeliveryFour finance agents working with our staff (Frontline growth plan)
PricingTied to days-to-pay, not hours worked
CapacityAdded by acquiring specialist legal billing providers

Timing

  • This is Phase 3 of our growth plan. It runs from about month 12 to month 30 after the plan date of Oct 6, 2026 (Frontline growth plan).
  • It follows Phase 1, which upgrades our service desk, and overlaps with Phase 2, which extends our service to mid-size firms.
  • Our approach for international clients comes later, in Phase 4. That phase includes acquired billing capability in the UK and Canada.

  • The context does not include current rejection rates or days-to-pay for our own clients. A baseline by client, built from billing-system data, would show the real starting point.
  • The context also does not define the four finance agents task by task. A service design document would settle that before any client pricing is set.

Days-to-pay pricing gives us a measurable reason to win more work from firms we already serve. The roadmap counts on about $25M of cumulative acquired revenue (est.) from MSP and revenue-cycle add-ons by month 24, while EBITDA growth carries the return on a purchase at about 12-15x (est.) (Frontline growth plan; Frontline public filings).

Next actions

  1. Pull a rejection-rate and days-to-pay baseline for a sample of current law-firm clients. This will test whether the 18% figure matches our own book.
  2. Define the scope of each of the four finance agents and the hand-off points to staff.
  3. Rank the billing acquisition screen (Helm360, The Garver Group, The Legal Billing Group) on fit, size and integration effort.
  4. Draft a days-to-pay pricing model and test it with two or three AM Law clients before the Phase 3 start.
markdown:
# How we handle eBilling and A/R

We support law-firm billing teams today. Our plan is to bring eBilling and accounts receivable together as one managed service, run partly by AI finance agents and priced on how quickly clients pay (Frontline growth plan).

## Why billing needs attention now

- Corporate clients increasingly use AI to review legal invoices.
- That review has pushed invoice rejection rates from 11% to 18% (Frontline growth plan).
- Each rejection slows cash collection and adds rework for the firm's billing staff.

## What the service will look like

| Element | How it works |
|---|---|
| Scope | eBilling submission, rejection handling and A/R follow-up in one service |
| Delivery | Four finance agents working with our staff (Frontline growth plan) |
| Pricing | Tied to days-to-pay, not hours worked |
| Capacity | Added by acquiring specialist legal billing providers |

## Timing

- This is Phase 3 of our growth plan. It runs from about month 12 to month 30 after the plan date of Oct 6, 2026 (Frontline growth plan).
- It follows Phase 1, which upgrades our service desk, and overlaps with Phase 2, which extends our service to mid-size firms.
- Our approach for international clients comes later, in Phase 4. That phase includes acquired billing capability in the UK and Canada.

## What we can't confirm yet

- The context does not include current rejection rates or days-to-pay for our own clients. A baseline by client, built from billing-system data, would show the real starting point.
- The context also does not define the four finance agents task by task. A service design document would settle that before any client pricing is set.

Days-to-pay pricing gives us a measurable reason to win more work from firms we already serve. The roadmap counts on about $25M of cumulative acquired revenue (est.) from MSP and revenue-cycle add-ons by month 24, while EBITDA growth carries the return on a purchase at about 12-15x (est.) (Frontline growth plan; Frontline public filings).

## Next actions

1. Pull a rejection-rate and days-to-pay baseline for a sample of current law-firm clients. This will test whether the 18% figure matches our own book.
2. Define the scope of each of the four finance agents and the hand-off points to staff.
3. Rank the billing acquisition screen (Helm360, The Garver Group, The Legal Billing Group) on fit, size and integration effort.
4. Draft a days-to-pay pricing model and test it with two or three AM Law clients before the Phase 3 start.
